name: abandoned rusted car facing south seen from above: trunk, roof and hood tops with cracked glass, front grille and bumper below
label: wasteland_ruins/car-rust-v

answer.evidence: The car body is mostly a tall stack of horizontal top surfaces: trunk (rows 2-11), rear glass (11-14), roof (15-27, with a light edge line at row 15), windshield (28-31) and hood (32-40). Each part is separated by an edge line or dark band. Below the hood, a darker band at rows 41-44 leads into a grille (about rows 42-44) and a bumper (rows 45-47). Together these give a vertical south face of about 6 rows. The drawing leans strongly toward top-down, but it has a front face of 3 or more rows and clear top planes. The dark strips at the left and right edges are wheels and arches, not receding side faces.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 15 visible tones per tile, which is in line with the stall (17), well (20) and hedge (9). Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted dark green-grey, not a black sticker line. Near-flat coverage is 25%, the highest on the board (stall 13%, others 0%), and by eye the large teal body panels (hood, roof, trunk) read as broad, mostly flat fields. Rust speckles are scattered thinly on top. The glass cracks are only faint lines, and the grille and bumper are small and simple. Each material ramp shows about 3-4 steps (teal body, dark window, rust spots), compared with the 5-6 that Beodeul references use. There is no per-panel highlight/shadow modeling, panel edges are sparse, and there is little grain on the body. Overall it is competent and not a sticker, but it is flatter and thinner in shading than the stall and well, so it falls short of the bar.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a teal-grey car seen from above with rust speckles, a cracked windshield and a grille. Near-flat coverage is 25%, against 0-13% for the references, so some large areas are flat. The roof and hood panels are big areas of one teal-grey with little grain, and the rust dots are sparse and scattered rather than shaded into the material. The body has only about 3-4 lightness steps (highlight edge, base, shade, dark edge), shallower than the 5-6 steps on the stall awning and well roof. The structure is clear, but the panels need more tile-by-tile texture and a wider value ramp to match the reference richness. Flat fills and shallow body shading make it fall short, so it fails.
